title: Record injection sequence
purpose: Record the actual injection order transcribed from an instrument source record for an analytical batch.
summary: Transcribe the instrument’s actual injection order. Analysts and administrators can record sequences for open or closed analytical batches.

tasks.title: Transcribe an instrument run
steps: Enter the instrument run identifier in [[Run reference]] and identify the record you transcribed in [[Source reference]].
Enter every position, kind and instrument label in [[Injections (one per line)]].
Select [[Record injection sequence]] to save version 1 and open it.

tasks.title: Fix an input error
steps: Read the error beside the field and check that entry against the source record.
Correct the entry and select [[Record injection sequence]] again.

good_to_know: Use the source record that shows what the instrument ran. The run-list CSV describes planned batch membership.
Keep commas and quotes in a label as shown on the instrument. The first two commas separate the position and kind from the label.
You can record evidence after batch closure. Closure freezes which samples and QC samples are in the batch.
To fix a saved transcription, open its current version and choose Correct injection sequence.

items.label: Run reference
items.description: Required instrument run identifier, up to 120 characters. The reference must be unique within the batch and remains fixed across corrections.

items.label: Source reference
items.description: Required identifier for the source record, up to 240 characters. Use a reference that helps staff find the source, such as the instrument run log or export name.

items.label: Injections (one per line)
items.description: Required complete transcription, with 1 to 200 positions entered in order without gaps or repeats, starting at 1. Enter position,kind,label with no header. For example, enter 1,verification,SYN-CCV and then 2,sample,SYN-001 on the next line. Kinds are sample, verification, standard, blank and other. Labels require 1 to 120 printable characters with at least one non-space character. Everything after the second comma is the literal label, including spaces, commas and quote marks.

sections.title: Actions and access

items.label: Record injection sequence
items.description: Save a new run as version 1 with your account and the current laboratory time, then open the sequence. Correct validation errors and try again. The form keeps the entered values.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Return to the analytical batch or close the form dialog without saving.

paragraphs: Analysts and administrators can use this form. Staff with other application roles can inspect saved sequences. The form is available for analytical batches only.
